dervis-irab:1-21.t:
* I'rab:
(وَاللَّيْلِ إِذا يَغْشى وَالنَّهارِ إِذا تَجَلَّى وَما خَلَقَ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثى إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّى)
The wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive; (والليل) is genitive through the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear". (إذا) is an adverb of mere time, free of any conditional sense, attached to the verb of the oath; the discussion of it has already preceded. The clause (يغشى) is in the position of a genitive, as the adverb is annexed to it. (والنهار إذا تجلى) is conjoined to the preceding clause. (وما خلق): (ما) is either maṣdar (verbal noun) or relative, conjoined to what preceded. (إن سعيكم لشتى) is the answer to the oath: He, Glory be to Him, swore that the deeds of His servants are (شتى), the plural of (شتيت). Whatever is diverse and mutually different is called (شتى) because of the distance between its parts; (الشتات) is separation. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "(شتّ) (شتّا), of the pattern of ḍaraba, when it is scattered; the noun is (الشتات); and (شيء شتيت), of the pattern of (كريم), is something scattered; (قوم شتى), of the pattern fuʿlā, are people scattered; (جاءوا أشتاتا) is the same; and (شتان ما بينهما) means 'how far apart they are'." (إن) and its noun, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and (شتى) is the khabar (predicate) of (إن).
(فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطى وَاتَّقى وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنى فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرى)
The fāʾ is resumptive, and (أما) is a particle of condition and elaboration. (من) is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (أعطى) is the ṣila (relative clause). (واتقى) is conjoined to (أعطى); (وصدّق بالحسنى) is likewise conjoined. (فسنيسّره): the fāʾ is the connector of the apodosis, the sīn is for futurity, and (نيسّره) is an imperfect verb, with a latent agent and a direct object. (لليسرى) and the preposition are attached to (نيسّره).
(وَأَمَّا مَنْ بَخِلَ وَاسْتَغْنى وَكَذَّبَ بِالْحُسْنى فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرى)
Conjoined to what preceded, parallel to it in its i'rab.
(وَما يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مالُهُ إِذا تَرَدَّى)
The wāw is a conjunction and (ما) is negative. It is also permissible for it to be interrogative, in the sense of denial, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of (يغني), i.e. "what kind of benefit will it benefit?". Some parse it as a fronted direct object, with the implied sense "what thing will it avail?". (يغني) is an imperfect nominative verb; (عنه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يغني); (ماله) is the agent. (إذا) is an adverb of mere time attached to (يغني), and the clause (تردى) is in the position of a genitive, as the adverb is annexed to it.
Ibn Khālawayh has a fine discussion of (تردى). He said: "(تردّى) is a past verb, and its verbal noun is (تردّى يتردّى تردّيا), so he is (متردّ); from it comes the saying of the Exalted (والمتردية والنطيحة). One says: (تردّى) into a well, or into a chasm, or into a perdition, when he fell into it. And one says: (ردي زيد يردى ردى) when he perished, and (أرداه الله يرديه إرداء). And one says: (ردى الفرس يردي رديانا). al-Aṣmaʿī said: I asked Muntajiʿ ibn Nabhān about the (رديان) of the horse, and he said: it is its running between its (آريّه) and its (متمعّكه). The (آري) is the (آخيّة), that is, the manger; and the (متمعّك) is the place in which it rolls. The (آري) is of the pattern fāʿūl, so named because it holds the animal back; one says (تأريت بالمكان) when you stayed in it and were held back in it." al-Mubarrad said: "Two things are said about it: one, 'when he falls into the Fire'; the other, 'when he dies'; and is it a form of the pattern tafaʿʿala derived from (الردى)?"
(إِنَّ عَلَيْنا لَلْهُدى)
A resumptive statement, delivered to inform them that it rests upon Him, Glory be to Him, by the requirement of His wisdom, to make clear the guidance as distinct from error. (إن) is a particle resembling the verb; (علينا) is its fronted khabar (predicate); the lām is for emphasis; and (الهدى) is the postponed noun of (إن).
(وَإِنَّ لَنا لَلْآخِرَةَ وَالْأُولى)
The wāw is a conjunction, and what follows it is conjoined to what preceded, parallel to it in i'rab.
(فَأَنْذَرْتُكُمْ ناراً تَلَظَّى)
The fāʾ is conjoined to something implied, i.e. "whoever seeks this world and the next from other than their true Owner, who is Allah, has missed the way and strayed from the right path". (أنذرتكم) is a past verb, an agent and a direct object; (نارا) is a second direct object; and the clause (تلظى) is an adjective of (نارا). (تلظى) is an imperfect verb, the original being (تتلظى). The wording of Ibn Khālawayh is excellent, and it is: "(تلظى) is an imperfect verb, the original being (تتلظى), and Ibn Masʿūd indeed read it so. Ibn Kathīr read:
(نارا تّلظى) with the assimilation of the tāʾ, meaning (نارا تتلظى). Had (تلظى) been a past verb, it would have been said (تلظت), because (النار) is feminine. The verbal noun is (تلظّت تتلظى تلظّيا), so she is (متلظية). Among the names of Hell are said to be Saqar, Jahannam, al-Jaḥīm and Lazā; we seek refuge in Allah from it. These names are definite and are diptotes, because of feminine gender and definiteness."
(لا يَصْلاها إِلَّا الْأَشْقَى)
(لا) is negative; (يصلاها) is an imperfect nominative verb, and the hāʾ is the direct object; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (الأشقى) is the agent of (يصلاها).
(الَّذِي كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى)
(الذي) is an adjective of (الأشقى); the clause (كذب) has no grammatical position, because it is a ṣila; and (تولى) is conjoined to (كذب), falling within the scope of the ṣila.
(وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا الْأَتْقَى الَّذِي يُؤْتِي مالَهُ يَتَزَكَّى)
The wāw is a conjunction, and the sīn is a particle of the future, brought for emphasis. (يجنبها) is an imperfect nominative verb with a direct object; (الأتقى) is the agent; (الذي) is an adjective; the clause (يؤتي) is a ṣila; (ماله) is a direct object; and (يتزكى) is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent. The clause is either a badal (substitute) for (يؤتي), in which case it has no grammatical position, since it falls within the scope of the ṣila of (الذي); or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of (يؤتي), i.e. "purifying himself by it in the sight of Allah".
(وَما لِأَحَدٍ عِنْدَهُ مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ تُجْزى إِلَّا ابْتِغاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ الْأَعْلى)
The wāw is a conjunction and (ما) is negative. (لأحد), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (عنده) is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl. (من) is a redundant preposition of the genitive, and (نعمة) is genitive by (من) in form, nominative in position, as mubtadaʾ. (إلا) is a particle of exception in the sense of (لكن) ("but"), and (ابتغاء) is excepted from a different class, for it is a disconnected exception, because seeking the face of his Lord is not of the class of favour; that is: "no one has with him any favour, except the seeking of the face of his Lord". It is better to parse (ابتغاء) as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), because the meaning is: he gives his wealth only for the seeking of the face of his Lord, not in recompense for a favour. (ابتغاء) was also read in the nominative, on the dialect of one who says (ما في الدار أحد إلا حمار) ("there is no one in the house but a donkey"), and then it is a badal for the position of (من نعمة). He said:
وبلدة ليس بها أنيس ... إلا اليعافير وإلا العيس
(Many a land in which there is no companion, except the gazelles and except the white camels.)
And Bishr ibn Abī Ḥāzim said:
أضحت خلاء قفارا لا أنيس بها ... إلا الجآذر والظلمان تختلف
(She became empty, a wasteland, with no companion in her, except the gazelle-calves and the ostriches, going back and forth.)
The detail of this rule will come in the section on Benefits.
(وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضى)
The wāw is a conjunction, and the lām is the answer of an implied oath, i.e. "By Allah, he will surely be satisfied". (سوف) is a particle of the future, and (يرضى) is an imperfect verb whose agent is "he", referring to Abū Bakr, about whom the verse was revealed when he bought Bilāl, who was being tortured for his faith, from his master Umayya ibn Khalaf, and freed him. The disbelievers said: "He only did that because of some favour Bilāl had done him."

* Benefits:
When the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), which is where the excepted is not part of that from which it is excepted, on condition that what precedes (إلا) indicates what is excepted: if it is not possible to direct the governing word onto the excepted, the accusative is obligatory for the excepted, by agreement, as in (ما زاد هذا المال إلا ما نقص): (ما) is maṣdar and (نقص) is its ṣila, and their position is accusative as an exception. It is not permissible to make it nominative as a badal from the agent, because the governing word cannot be directed onto it, since one does not say (زاد النقص). Likewise (ما نفع زيد إلا ما ضرّ), since one does not say (ما نفع الضرّ). But if it is possible to direct the governing word onto the excepted, as in (ما قام القوم إلا حمارا), since it is sound to say (قام حمار), then the Hijazis make the accusative obligatory, because badal is not truly sound there, as the excepted is not of the class of that from which it is excepted; and on this is the reading of the Seven: (ما لهم به من علم إلا اتباع الظن). Tamīm prefer the nominative and permit following, and they read (إلا اتباع الظن) in the nominative as a badal for (العلم) with regard to its position. From this is the saying of Jarān al-ʿAwd ʿĀmir ibn al-Ḥārith:
وبلدة ليس بها أنيس ... إلا اليعافير وإلا العيس
(Many a land in which there is no companion, except the gazelles and except the white camels.)
He made (اليعافير) and (العيس) a badal for (الأنيس); the second (إلا) is a confirmation of the first. (اليعافير) is the plural of (يعفور), which is the calf of the wild cow; and (العيس), with kasra on the ʿayn, is the plural of (عيساء), like (البيض) the plural of (بيضاء); they are white camels whose whiteness is mixed with some reddishness. Sībawayh mentioned two explanations for the nominative: one, that they construed it according to the meaning, since the intended thing is the excepted: one who says (ما في الدار أحد إلا حمار) means "there is in the house only a donkey", and the mention of (أحد) became a confirmation, to make known that there is no human there; then what he intended by mentioning the donkey was made a badal for (أحد). The second explanation is that he made the donkey the "person" of the house, that is, the one who takes the place of a human in the house.
Ibn Yaʿīsh said: "Of the disconnected exception is the saying of the Exalted: (وما لأحد عنده من نعمة تجزى إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه الأعلى ولسوف يرضى). The Banū Tamīm read it in the nominative, and make seeking the face of Him, Glory be to Him, a favour of theirs with Him."
